title: Interleaved affinity prober for attention kernel selection and NCCL dovetailing
creator: Lucas Meyer
description:
Problem statement: Multi-GPU prefill/decode workloads experience tail latency spikes caused by poor coordination between attention kernel choices and cross-device communication windows. On heterogeneous hardware and mixed model mixes, naive synchronized kernel election (e.g., everyone choosing the heaviest but fastest single-GPU kernel) creates NCCL contention and end-to-end latency regressions.

Goal: Implement an interleaved affinity prober that probabilistically probes alternative attention kernel paths per-microbatch and steers subsequent microbatches to kernel+comm pairings that maximize achieved overlap (compute vs NCCL) while preserving token throughput and output determinism constraints for pinned workloads.

Design summary:
- Lightweight probe layer in the runtime scheduler that tags a small fraction of microbatches (1-5%) with alternate kernel + comm-plan candidates. Probes record latency, NCCL overlap, and SM utilization.
- Affinity table per model variant and topology records rolling-window scores for kernel+plan combinations (keys: device topology fingerprint, model-arch-profile, sequence-length-bucket).
- Probabilistic selection: use a softmax over affinity scores with an exploration factor that decays as confidence grows. This avoids synchronized oscillation across GPUs.
- NCCL dovetailing heuristics: for plans that enable overlapped allreduce/allgather windows, the scheduler introduces micro-offsets (microbatch interleaving) across replica groups to stagger collective start times, exploiting natural bandwidth smoothing.
- Safety controls: fallbacks to conservative kernel (deterministic path) when KV-cache or reproducibility flags are set; global rate limit for probe traffic; circuit-breaker on increased error rates.

Why this is different from prior approaches: Instead of global deterministic hand-offs or static topology heuristics, this design embraces measured, probabilistic exploration combined with micro-offset scheduling to discover high-overlap operating points dynamically per-customer workload mix. It specifically targets skew-tolerance when links are heterogeneous (e.g., mixed NVLink/NVSwitch islands).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements interleaved affinity prober that can be toggled by model route config
Affinity table persists scores for a model-topology-seqlen bucket and updates on probes
End-to-end P95 latency for our multi-GPU prefill benchmark decreases by >=12% in heterogeneous link tests compared to baseline with static kernels
NCCL busy time overlap increases (measured by overlapping NCCL wall-time / total latency) by >=15% without reducing overall throughput
Feature has a runtime flag and per-customer rollout plan with safe fallback to deterministic kernel path
Telemetry surfaces probe rate, selected kernel+plan, overlap fraction, and a drift alert when probe-selected plans degrade
comments: 2025-02-20 - Lucas Meyer: Initial spike analysis attached in Confluence. Observed synchronized allgather start events causing 40-200ms tails on 8-GPU racks with mixed NVLink. Proposed probabilistic probing instead of global reconfigure.

2025-02-22 - Aisha Khan: Implemented first-pass probe sampler and in-memory affinity table. Running nightly against multi-topology canary; early signals show 6-8% P95 improvement but noisy on high-variance seq-len workloads.
2025-02-24 - Maya Patel (PM): Confirming customer-impacted routes to include enterprise clients using dedicated pools. Prioritize safety and opt-outs for private deployments.

2025-02-26 - Ramon Silva (SRE): Observed a transient increase in CUDA kernel launch variance when probing rate was 10%. Recommend default probe to 2% and add a backoff when variance exceeds threshold.

2025-02-28 - Aisha Khan: Added micro-offset interleaver and probabilistic softmax selector. Needs perf run and validation of KV-cache determinism behavior. TODO: add unit test for affinity table decay logic and write dashboard widget for overlap fraction per-route.
